neighbours.label: The word justified as a predicate evaluating a belief or action
fire: The committee decided that the intervention was justified by the evidence.
Her belief is justified if the witnesses are reliable.
The philosopher asks whether our confidence is justified in this case.
Their refusal to cooperate was justified under the circumstances.
A punishment can be justified only when the accused is responsible.
The critic argues that such anger is justified after a betrayal.
The assumption would be justified if the measurements agreed.
We must explain why this exception is justified on moral grounds.
quiet: The committee decided that the intervention was supported by the evidence.
Her belief is defensible if the witnesses are reliable.
The philosopher asks whether our confidence is reasonable in this case.
Their refusal to cooperate was defensible under the circumstances.
A punishment can be legitimate only when the accused is responsible.
The critic argues that such anger is understandable after a betrayal.
The assumption would be sound if the measurements agreed.
We must explain why this exception is acceptable on moral grounds.

notes: Card-only hypothesis from the strongest example and several evaluative predicates. Other peaks include diluted, so this is a narrow candidate trigger, not a complete account. Sentences authored by Codex, not Bonsai.
